tools.name: read-dialog
tools.description: Read the dialogs the server has opened on screen, with their title, body and the buttons they offer, and the point at which each was closed again. The bot cannot press those buttons: the packet that answers a dialog is serialised from a definition that does not match 26.1, and a server drops the connection rather than read it. Repeats are collapsed, so each line is a change. A HUD drawn in custom fonts arrives as several pieces separated by " | ", each tagged with the font that names it.

bot.description: Bot name given to join-server. Optional while exactly one bot is connected.

tools.name: join-server
tools.description: Send a bot into a Minecraft server and wait until it has spawned. A bot already running under this name is used as it is; otherwise one is started, which in a cluster means the operator creates it and takes a few seconds longer. A failure says how far it got, because a bot that never started and a server that refused the login have different fixes.

name.description: Name used to address this bot in other tools

host.description: Server host or Kubernetes service name to connect to

version.description: Force a protocol version instead of auto-detecting

owner.description: Free-form label recording who asked for this bot. Defaults to the authenticated caller.

kind.description: Which kind of bot to start when none by this name is running. "fabric" is a real Minecraft client: it can take a screenshot and press a dialog button, and costs several times the memory for it. (default: mineflayer)

minecraftVersion.description: Minecraft version for a bot that has to be started. A fabric client is built against one version; a mineflayer bot negotiates at runtime and ignores this. (default: 26.1.2)
